title: He asked God for a sign.
paragraphs:
He asked God for a sign.
Then he asked again.
And God answered… again.
That alone should make you pause.
Because the story of Gideon’s fleece in Judges 6 is not about a fearless hero.
It’s about a man shaking inside.
A man hiding.
A man who felt completely unqualified for the calling of God.
And maybe—if we’re honest—that’s exactly why this story hits so hard.
Because Gideon is a mirror.
And in many ways… we are Gideon.
The night fear met the voice of God
Israel was crushed.
The Midianites raided their land year after year. Crops destroyed. Livestock stolen. Villages stripped bare. People hiding in caves just to survive.
Imagine waking up every day wondering if everything you built would be taken before sunset.
That was Gideon’s world.
So when the angel of the Lord appeared, Gideon wasn’t standing tall in a battlefield.
He was hiding in a winepress, secretly threshing wheat so the enemy wouldn’t see him.
And then God said something that must have sounded almost unbelievable:
“The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.” — Judges 6:12
Mighty warrior?
The man was hiding.
Yet heaven saw something Gideon couldn’t see yet.
And that’s how God often works.
He doesn’t call us based on our current strength.
He calls us based on His purpose.
Gideon’s question that echoes in every human heart
Gideon answered honestly.

Not like a polished hero.
Not like a perfect believer.
But like someone who had questions.
“If the LORD is with us, why has all this happened?” — Judges 6:13
Have you ever asked that?
Why the struggle?
Why the delay?
Why the silence?

Faith doesn’t mean you never ask questions.
It means you bring those questions to God instead of away from Him.
And God did something remarkable.
He didn’t rebuke Gideon.
He called him anyway.
The trembling obedience
Before Gideon ever touched a battlefield, God told him to do something far more personal.
Destroy the altar of Baal in his own father’s house.
That meant confronting idolatry in his own family.
So Gideon did it.
But he did it at night, because he was afraid.
Let that sink in.
God used a man who obeyed while trembling.
And maybe that’s a word for someone reading this.
Courage isn’t always loud.
Sometimes courage looks like obedience in the dark… while your heart is racing.
The fleece that revealed God’s patience
Even after obeying, Gideon was still unsure.
So he asked for reassurance.
He laid out a fleece and said:
“If you will save Israel by my hand as you have promised…” — Judges 6:36
First sign:
Dew on the fleece only.
Dry ground.
God answered.
But Gideon still felt weak.
So he asked again.
Second sign:
Dry fleece.
Wet ground.
And again…
God answered.
Think about that for a moment.
God could have rebuked him.
God could have said, “Didn’t I already speak?”
Instead, God stooped down into Gideon’s weakness and gave reassurance.
That’s not weakness on God’s part.
That’s mercy.
The deeper message most people miss
Many people read this story and think it teaches us to test God with signs.
But the real focus isn’t the fleece.
The real focus is God’s patience with fragile faith.
Gideon wavers.
God stays faithful.
Gideon fears.
God reassures.
Gideon doubts.
God continues speaking.
The hero of Judges 6 isn’t Gideon.
It’s God.
But the greatest reassurance came centuries later
Because Gideon’s fleece wasn’t the ultimate sign.
It was only a shadow of something greater.
One day, God would give humanity a sign that would never fade.
Not dew on wool.
Not fire on a rock.
But a Savior on a cross.
When Jesus Christ died and rose again, God gave the clearest message the universe has ever heard:
You are not abandoned.
You are not forgotten.
And grace is stronger than your fear.
The cross is God’s ultimate reassurance.
So if you feel like Gideon today…
If you feel small.
Hidden.
Unqualified.
Uncertain.
Hear this clearly:
God still calls ordinary people.
God still strengthens weak faith.
God still walks with trembling servants.
And the same God who met Gideon in a winepress is the same God who meets you right where you are.
You don’t have to be fearless.
You just have to be willing.
Because the God who begins the calling…
Is the God who provides the strength.
“Surely I will be with you.” — Judges 6:16
That promise changed Gideon’s story.
And through Jesus Christ…
That promise still stands today.
🔥 If this message spoke to you, pause and reflect:

• Have you ever felt like Gideon—called but unsure?
• What fear has been holding you back from obedience?
• Where might God already be asking you to trust Him?
You never know whose faith might be strengthened by a single reminder of God’s patience.
Because sometimes the person hiding in the winepress…
Is the very person God plans to use to change the battlefield.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
